title: Distribution-free improper learning of two unrestricted halfspaces
formal: Is there a single randomized learner that, for every distribution \(D\) on \(\{0,1\}^n\), every target \(f\) expressible as the intersection of two integer-weight halfspaces of total description length at most a supplied bound \(B\), and every rational \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\), uses only independent labeled examples from \(D\) to output a Boolean circuit \(H\) with \(\Pr_{x\sim D}[H(x)\ne f(x)]\le\varepsilon\) with probability at least \(2/3\), in time polynomial in \(n+B+\lceil1/\varepsilon\rceil+\operatorname{len}(\varepsilon)\)?
definitions: A halfspace is \(h(x)=1\) exactly when \(\sum_{i} w_{i} x_{i}\ge \theta\), with \(w_i,\theta\in\mathbb{Z}\) in signed binary; equality is positive. The target f is the conjunction of two such predicates. Its description length is the bit length of a list of both weight vectors and thresholds, using self-delimiting binary integers. The learner receives n and B in unary and a rational \(\varepsilon\) with \(0<\varepsilon <1/2\) in binary. It is promised that f has at least one such description of length at most B, but receives neither that description nor its weights. An example oracle returns independent pairs \((x,f(x))\) with x sampled from an arbitrary fixed distribution D on \(\{0,1\}^{n}\). The learner receives only these labeled examples and its own independent fair coins. Each oracle call costs at least \(n+1\) steps to receive its bits; all further work is charged in Turing-machine bit steps. Membership queries, advice and descriptions or probability evaluations of D are absent. There must be a fixed polynomial P such that on every random tape the running time, and hence sample count and output length, are bounded by \(P(n+B+\lceil1/\varepsilon\rceil+\operatorname{len}(\varepsilon))\). Output a deterministic Boolean circuit \(H:\{0,1\}^{n}\to \{0,1\}\) in the explicit \(\mathrm{AND}/\mathrm{OR}/\mathrm{NOT}\) basis. The success condition is \(\Pr_{\mathrm{samples,coins}}[\Pr_{x\sim D}[H(x)\ne f(x)]\le\varepsilon]\ge2/3\), uniformly over \(n,B,\varepsilon ,D\) and every promised f. Circuit evaluation costs polynomial time in its output encoding. The hypothesis need not be an intersection of halfspaces. Encoding an arbitrary deterministic polynomial-time evaluator by its Boolean circuit preserves this unrestricted efficient-output convention.

context_blocks.text: A single halfspace is efficiently learnable, but combining only two thresholds introduces a longstanding computational obstacle. Allowing an arbitrary output representation avoids the known hardness of proper learning.

The existing TCS-6544 explicitly assumes a positive margin and polynomial dependence on its reciprocal. This candidate instead concerns unrestricted integer-weight thresholds on the Boolean cube. The distinction affects the running time and cannot be hidden behind their similar titles.

why: Determine whether combining two elementary classifiers already defeats efficient distribution-free learning.
answer_criterion: Provide a Lean proof constructing and bounding a learner under all the stated quantifiers, or a Lean proof that none exists. Proper-learning hardness and statistical-query lower bounds do not exclude all allowed learners. A margin promise, a restricted input distribution or membership queries would change the problem.

progress.text: The source distinguishes proper-learning hardness from the unresolved unrestricted-output learning question.
Tiegel’s published hardness result still describes polynomial-time learning of two halfspaces as open; its lattice-based bound concerns a growing number of halfspaces.
A later preprint gives subexponential-time learning for arbitrary Boolean functions of a fixed number of halfspaces, without establishing polynomial time for the present two-halfspace target.

sentences: One threshold is efficiently learnable from labeled examples, but the target here combines two thresholds.
Examples follow any fixed distribution on the Boolean cube and no positive margin is promised.
The learner receives a bound on target description length and may output any efficiently evaluable classifier.
Hardness for proper learners or growing numbers of halfspaces does not settle this two-halfspace target.
The question asks for a uniform polynomial-time guarantee across all distributions and permitted target descriptions.
